title: Chromatic Legibility V2: define palette fallbacks, typographic scale deltas, and subpixel radius constraints for compact components
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Problem statement: In compact/dense surfaces (cards, compact tables, and small action bars) we observe multiple regressions after the last token rebake: (1) certain semantic accents fall below 3:1 at small sizes in high-AP contrast locales; (2) type scale deltas for compact form factor cause perceived visual wobble between 12px/13px size transitions; (3) subpixel corner rounding on low-DPI displays produces visible aliasing when combining the current radius tokens with the new elevation shadow stacks.

Goal: Produce a conservative, backwards-compatible token patch (Chromatic Legibility V2) that: (a) introduces a concise set of fallback color ramps for regionally-sensitive palettes, (b) defines a compact-mode typographic delta set (type token offsets) to stabilise micro-size transitions, and (c) adds subpixel-aware radius variants and shadow offsets to avoid aliasing artifacts. The change should ship with an automated migration script, visual diff dashboard, and staged rollout across component families (buttons, tables, charts) with a canary phase.

Scope: color palette fallbacks (semantic/neutral/accent), typographic scale deltas for compact mode, spacing/radius micro-variants (0.5px-aware), shadow/elevation micro-offsets for dense elevation stacks, token export and migration tooling, design documentation and dev integration notes.

Out-of-scope: full palette redesign, global density swap, or button chrome redesign; those will be tracked in follow-ups.
acceptance_criteria: Contrast: all primary and secondary interactive states meet WCAG 2.1 AA (4.5:1) for body and 3:1 for UI components where defined; automated contrast checks in CI must pass for token-driven components.
Typographic: compact type delta tokens defined as numeric offsets (e.g., text-xs-compact = text-xs - 1px where perceptually appropriate) and annotated in the token spec with usage guidance.

Radius/Shadow: introduce three subpixel-aware radius tokens (r-sub-0, r-sub-1, r-sub-2) and corresponding shadow-offset tokens to remove visible aliasing on common low-DPI screens; visual diffs show no new aliasing regressions.
Migration: one-click migration script that maps legacy token names to new tokens for buttons, tables, and charts, with a dry-run mode and a report of changed components.
Rollout: staged canary rollout plan documented with monitoring hooks (visual diff dashboard link, error/UX feedback form) and rollback criteria defined.
Docs & Examples: Confluence spec, Figma token page, and three example component previews (button, compact table row, micro-chart tooltip) published and linked in the ticket.
Engineering sign-off: ENG and PM review completed and a merged PR with token JSON and stylus/css variables in the tokens repo (or equivalent) exists.

Measurements: baseline and post-rollout metrics for perceived legibility (qualitative review) and token usage impact (token-change % by component) recorded in the console dashboard for the release window.
updates: 2025-11-10 - Maya Chen: Initial audit complete. Collected 78 examples across product surfaces where contrast or radius aliasing is visible. Generated spreadsheet with priority buckets (high/medium/low) and sample screenshots.

2025-11-22 - Design sync: Chose conservative approach to color ramps: add two local fallback steps rather than rebaking global neutrals. PM asked for migration script and rollback plan before any release.

2025-12-05 - Prototype: Implemented compact type delta tokens in Figma and produced micro-spec for token offsets. Shared with Engs for perf considerations — Ravi to follow up on rendering/rounding trade-offs.

2025-12-18 - Dev spike (ENG-2248): Engineering reports that 0.5px radius requires per-platform rounding tables; suggested we provide both logical (token-level) and platform mapping guidance. Added to acceptance criteria.

2026-01-04 - Accessibility review: a11y lead validated approach for accent fallback; two accent tokens still failing 3:1 for certain background mixes — we will bump those accents by 6% luminance in the patch.
2026-01-12 - Design review: PM and Charts lead requested example snapshots for micro-chart axis labels and sparklines; added to attachments and test matrix.

2026-01-20 - Engineering PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/tokens/pull/412 (token JSON + migration script dry-run). Dev reports one remaining issue: chart legend icons need an explicit neutral-contrast token mapping.
Next steps: finalize migration dry-run results, update chart legend mapping, schedule canary rollout for 2026-02-05, prepare rollback playbook.
